subject: SSQ: role-based access matrix & international transfer justification
messages:
From: Seema Patel <seema.patel@medtech.co>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps Team <legalops@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: SSQ kickoff - role matrix & cross-border transfer justification

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our vendor onboarding for MedTech Health we need a few specific artifacts to close our privacy review: a role-based access matrix that lists which subteams and roles (engineering, SRE, support) have access to PII categories; a short justification for any transfers outside the EU/US and the legal basis; and an updated data flow diagram showing where tokens, logs, and customer PII may transit.

Attached are our SSQ template and the current DataFlow_v1.drawio we have for context. Can you please provide the matrix and a brief transfer justification by EOD next week? We may need KMS/export evidence after that.

High level questions:
- Do you classify inference logs as PII when they contain identifiers?
- Which subprocessors handle encrypted backups and are any hosted in jurisdictions requiring additional SCC or assessment?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’re on a tight procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Seema Patel
Director, Vendor Risk
MedTech Health

Attachments: SSQ_Templates.pdf (pdf), DataFlow_v1.drawio (diagram)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Seema Patel <seema.patel@medtech.co>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SSQ kickoff - role matrix & cross-border transfer justification

Seema — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver a role-based access matrix and a written transfer justification by 2028-06-04 COB. Quick plan:

1) I’ll attach a first-pass role_matrix_v1.csv covering engineering, infra, SRE, support, and product; it will include access method (console/API), purpose, and approval owner.
2) Hannah will update our dataflow diagram to call out token stores, KV cache persistence, and export paths.
3) Marissa will draft the legal basis note for transfers (SCCs + documented legitimate interest/contractual necessity where relevant) and list subprocessors with regions.

Short answers inline:
- Inference logs: if logs contain persistent customer identifiers we treat them as PII; we have redaction and tokenization options and configurable retention.
- Subprocessors for encrypted backups: our backup provider (Azure Backup via partner) is listed in our subprocessor roster and has EU and US regions; we’ll flag any that are only in APAC for additional controls.

I’ve attached role_matrix_v1.csv and a short draft transfer_justification.md. These are preliminary — Hannah will follow up with a diagram update.

Next steps: please confirm if the CSV columns meet your template expectations or if you prefer a matrix in the SSQ template directly. Happy to hop on a quick call.

—Karthik
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: role_matrix_v1.csv (csv), transfer_justification.md (text)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Seema Patel <seema.patel@medtech.co>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SSQ kickoff - role matrix & cross-border transfer justification

Seema / team — I updated our internal dataflow to highlight three zones: Inference runtime (ephemeral, no persisted PII by default), Transient KV/prefix cache (configurable TTL), and Persistent stores (logs/metrics/backups). Please see attached redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio. Notes:

- PII classification: we treat user identifiers, patient IDs, and direct identifiers as PII. Generated outputs are contextual — customers can configure retention and redaction at the project level.
- Access controls: RBAC is enforced at the route and model level; engineering access to persistent stores requires approval and justification recorded in our access request system.
- Export playbook: we have an export/playback runbook for requested e-discovery or legal export; Marissa will attach the checklist separately.

I included inline callouts on the diagram for where KMS keys are used and which subprocessors handle backups (this will be in the subprocessor list). If you want, I can export a PNG to embed in the SSQ template.

Hannah
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio (diagram)

From: LegalOps Team <legalops@clientcorp.com>

Date: 2028-06-01T15:08:00Z
Subject: Fwd: SSQ follow-up - subprocessors and SCCs

Forwarding from our legal side — some clarifying questions before we finalize the SSQ: 

1) Please enumerate current subprocessors that could access backups, logs, or observability traces and provide region-by-region hosting.
2) For any subprocessor hosted outside the EU, confirm the mechanism (SCCs / adequacy / explicit consent) and attach executed SCCs where available.
3) If you rely on a third-party for KMS-backed key custody (HSM), provide the attestation or SOC document that demonstrates separation of key material.

On the classification point: Legal would prefer a short table mapping data category -> example fields -> retention default. Can you provide that as a one-pager?

Laura — can you confirm whether the role_matrix_v1.csv includes approval owners and whether it is exportable to the SSQ template?

Thanks,
LegalOps Team

LegalOps / Seema — thank you for the precise asks. Attached are the items we discussed: an updated role_matrix_v1.csv with approval owners and access methods, a one-page data classification table (pasted below and uploaded to the Drive), the redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio file, and a short transfer justification that confirms SCCs for EU outbound transfers and contractual necessity for certain US-hosted telemetry flows.

Summary of deliverables attached and links:
- role_matrix_v1.csv — includes columns: role, team, data_categories_accessed, access_method, approval_owner, justification
- data_classification_onepager.pdf — maps PII categories to example fields and default retention
- redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio — diagram with callouts for KMS and subprocessors
- transfer_justification.md — explains legal basis by flow and includes a list of subprocessors + region and which legal mechanism applies

Quick answers to your earlier bullets:
- Enumeration of subprocessors touching backups/logs: Azure Backup (US/EU), PartnerStorageCo (EU), ObservabilityInc (US, GDPR-compliant contract). For any APAC-only subprocessor we flagged, we will provide additional controls or an alternative follow-up.
- KMS custody: we use a customer-separable KMS model; Redwood holds zero-knowledge of customer-managed keys when configured. We can provide the HSM attestation or SOC excerpt under NDA; please confirm preferred routing.

Next steps: 1) I’ll share the Drive folder with the assembled artifacts and a short spreadsheet that maps each SSQ question to the supporting file. 2) If Legal needs executed SCCs, Marissa will coordinate signature routing (DocuSign link below). 3) Proposed 30-min closure call: 2028-06-05 09:00 PT.
